_about: Component spec for pos-toggle-btn (style/pos-toggle-btn.css). Built 2026-09-04 as a brand-new, standalone component (Figma link + screenshot) — a plain on/off switch with no label/card wrapper, distinct from Switch button (which is a full-width labeled card) and Segmented button (multi-option pill). Note: style/pos-toggle.css already existed under a very similar name, but it is entirely docs-site-scoped (.styleguide-toggle*, the docs page's own theme-toggle pill) — not a real DS component, so this new component was placed in its own pos-toggle-btn.css file rather than reusing or renaming that one, to avoid conflating the two. Four states: off (--pos-color-content-icon, 'Graphic Normal'), on (--pos-color-interactive, 'Graphic Interactive'), off+disabled (--pos-color-content-icon-disabled, 'Graphic Disabled'), on+disabled (--pos-color-button-primary-disabled-background, 'Button Prim Bg Disabled' — neutral grey in dark mode) — all 4 track colors are real, already-existing tokens exactly matching the user's own token names. The thumb stays a single consistent color across all 4 states (--pos-color-page-background, theme-reactive white/dark-surface), following the same established pattern as Switch button's own toggle thumb (pos-switch-card.css) rather than a hardcoded white. Regenerate spec-toggle-btn.liquid via the Node regen snippet (RULES.md §6.4) if this file changes. 2026-09-04: added a dedicated Focus state — --pos-color-focused only ever applies during :focus-visible, so it was removed from shared.layout (previously listed under every other state) and now lives only in this new state (same issue and fix as Tab). 2026-10-02: props list added (was empty) from the real CSS classes / attributes. 2026-10-02: hover added in both states (it had none) — tokens listed in the off / on states with a hover role. Disabled checked fill/frame borrows the primary button disabled tokens (--pos-color-button-primary-disabled-background / -frame) — documented exception to RULES.md 2.2, see COMPONENT-RULES.md.
name: Toggle button
description: A standalone on/off switch — no label or card wrapper. Use Switch button instead when the toggle needs a full-width label and description.
whenToUse: A single, standalone on/off setting inline with other content (e.g. next to a label you already control elsewhere, or inside a table cell).
Building a custom control layout where Switch button's fixed label/icon/card structure doesn't fit.
whenNotToUse: A full-width labeled setting row — use Switch button instead, it already includes the label, optional icon, and card styling.
Choosing one of 3+ mutually exclusive options — use Segmented button instead.
do: Always pair with a visible or programmatically-associated label (e.g. wrap in your own <label>, or use aria-label/aria-labelledby) — the track alone has no accessible name.
Use role="switch" on the checkbox input, not just type="checkbox" alone.
dont: Use as a substitute for Switch button when a label and description are needed — build that with Switch button, not by manually adding text next to this component.
Render more than one visual state at once — only one of Off/On/Off-disabled/On-disabled applies to a given instance.
accessibility: role="switch" on the <input type="checkbox"> announces it as a two-state switch, not a plain checkbox, to assistive technology.
The visible focus ring only appears via :focus-visible, so it does not show on a plain mouse click.

props.name: checked
props.description: On / off state. The input is a real checkbox with role="switch", so the state is announced and keyboard-operable (Space) without extra JS.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Not operable; the track uses the disabled colors in both the on and the off state.

props.name: accessible name
props.type: aria-label on the input, or a visible <label for>
props.description: The switch has no text of its own — give it a name that says what it turns on (e.g. aria-label="Email notifications").

layout.role: Track and thumb corner radius (fully pill-shaped/circular)

thumb.role: Thumb color — consistent across all 4 states, same pattern as Switch button's own toggle thumb

tokens.role: Track on hover (off) — one step stronger than the resting track
Hover frame, 2px off the track — only visible in high contrast, where the track color cannot get stronger
Track on hover (on) — the interactive hover step
Hover frame, 2px off the track — only visible in high contrast
